findings: Owner request 2026-11-09: practice long questions for Chapter 21 in the same format as the Physics 11 chapter practice (English and Roman Urdu), written from the chapter; not printed in the book. 24 questions numbered 1-24; by section: 21.1 2, 21.2 2, 21.3 2, 21.4 4, 21.5 2, 21.6 1, 21.7 3, 21.8 2, 21.11 2, 21.12 2, 21.13 2.

12 pairs (theory 5 marks + numerical 3 marks) covering luminosity and the Stefan-Boltzmann law, radiant flux intensity and the inverse-square law, standard candles, blackbody radiation, Wien's displacement law, the radius of a star, absorption spectra and blue shift, cosmic redshift, Hubble's law and the Big Bang, atmospheric circulation (specific angular momentum, Coriolis effect, cells), Earth's energy budget and the poles-equator imbalance, and salinity, density and thermohaline circulation. Numericals use new values, recomputed in Python. Book corrections followed: r in F = L/4πr² is the distance from the star; Z = Δλ/λ ≈ Δf/f ≈ v/c; poleward air runs ahead of the ground while equatorward air lags behind; cosmic microwave background as the blackbody example.
Every question carries a book_ref (topic id and exact words of that topic's English lesson), verified by tools.py.
The Roman Urdu file has the same checkpoints, order and book_refs; each prompt keeps the English question with the Roman Urdu meaning in brackets.
Drafts for the academic review (second-person review before publication).
